page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs based on the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 12 physical cores and a single thread per core. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression also show poor throughput. However, the 12 dedicated cores deliver average multi-core performance, as demonstrated by middle-tier results in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory bandwidth remains average for both cached and uncached read/write operations, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is its modest single-threaded execution speed, which limits its effectiveness for latency-sensitive, single-core workloads. Qualitatively, the instance offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-intensive applications that can leverage parallel processing across its 12 dedicated cores without requiring local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is appropriate for workloads such as database operations, Redis caching, and moderate multi-threaded data processing, where the 96.0 GB memory capacity prevents out-of-memory bottlenecks.
